hook.line: English has one word for both jobs: "which". In Spanish you have to decide whether you are pointing back at a whole event or at one particular thing, and the answer changes the word.
hook.es: No vino, lo que me molestó.
hook.en: He didn't come, which annoyed me.

examples.es: No vino, lo que me molestó.
examples.en: He didn't come, which annoyed me.

examples.es: La casa en la que vivo es vieja.
examples.en: The house I live in is old.

examples.es: El café cerró, lo que preocupó a todos.
examples.en: The café closed, which worried everyone.

examples.es: La mujer con la que hablé es periodista.
examples.en: The woman I spoke with is a journalist.

examples.es: Nos quedamos sin plata, lo cual es un problema.
examples.en: We ran out of money, which is a problem.

examples.es: La calle por la que caminamos es muy vieja.
examples.en: The street we walked along is very old.

rule:
If "which" points back at a whole situation (he didn't come, the café closed), use *lo que* (or *lo cual*). *Lo* is neutral because a situation has no gender.

If it points at a noun, use *el que*, *la que*, *los que* or *las que*, matching that noun: *la casa en la que vivo*.

Any preposition goes in front: *en la que*, *con la que*, *por la que*. English can leave it at the end ("the house I live in"); Spanish cannot.
smallPrint: Teachers call this a relative pronoun whose antecedent is either a clause (*lo que*) or a noun (*el que*).

readAndPick.es: No vino, lo que me molestó.
options: He didn't come, which annoyed me.
The man who annoyed me didn't come.
He didn't come because I was annoyed.

readAndPick.es: La casa en la que vivo es vieja.
options: I live, which is old.
The house I live in is old.
The old house is where he lives.

readAndPick.es: Vale llegó tarde, lo que no me sorprendió.
options: Vale, who didn't surprise me, arrived late.
Vale arrived late because she didn't surprise me.
Vale arrived late, which didn't surprise me.

readAndPick.es: La mujer con la que hablé es periodista.
options: The woman I spoke with is a journalist.
The woman who spoke to me is a journalist.
I spoke with a woman, which is a journalist.

readAndPick.es: El carro en el que llegó es viejo.
options: The car that arrived is old.
The car he arrived in is old.
He arrived, which made the car old.

readAndPick.es: Altamira quiere comprar la cuadra, lo que no me gusta.
options: Altamira wants to buy the block that I don't like.
Altamira, who doesn't like the block, wants to buy it.
Altamira wants to buy the block, which I don't like.

readAndPick.es: La calle por la que caminamos es muy vieja.
options: The street we walked along is very old.
We walked, which is very old.
The street we walked is very old.

readAndPick.es: Nos quedamos sin plata, lo cual es un problema.
options: We ran out of money, which is a problem.
The money we ran out of is a problem.
We have a problem with the money.

readAndPick.es: El hombre del que hablas es Hernando.
options: The man who talks to you is Hernando.
The man you are talking about is Hernando.
The man you are talking about was Hernando.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *lo que* or *la que* and type the whole sentence: *Tomás no firmó, ___ molestó a Altamira.*
yourTurn.answer: Tomás no firmó, lo que molestó a Altamira.
yourTurn.why: *Lo que* points back at the whole event: Tomás not signing.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *lo que* or *la que* and type the whole sentence: *La casa en ___ vivo es vieja.*
yourTurn.answer: La casa en la que vivo es vieja.
yourTurn.why: *Casa* is a feminine noun, so *la que*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: The café closed, which worried everyone.
yourTurn.answer: El café cerró, lo que preocupó a todos.
accept: El café cerró, lo cual preocupó a todos.
yourTurn.why: "Which" points back at the closing, so *lo que*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: The woman I spoke with is a journalist.
yourTurn.answer: La mujer con la que hablé es periodista.
yourTurn.why: *Mujer* is feminine, and *con* goes before *la que*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: The street we walked along is very old.
yourTurn.answer: La calle por la que caminamos es muy vieja.
yourTurn.why: *Calle* is feminine, and *por* goes in front.

yourTurn.prompt: Join the ideas: *Vale llegó tarde.* Add "which didn't surprise me". Say: Vale arrived late, which didn't surprise me.
yourTurn.answer: Vale llegó tarde, lo que no me sorprendió.
accept: Vale llegó tarde, lo cual no me sorprendió.
yourTurn.why: The comment is about the whole event, so *lo que*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: The car he arrived in is old.
yourTurn.answer: El carro en el que llegó es viejo.
yourTurn.why: *Carro* is masculine, so *el que*, with *en* in front.

pitfalls.wrong: La casa que vivo es vieja.
pitfalls.right: La casa en la que vivo es vieja.
pitfalls.why: Almost. Spanish needs the preposition, and it goes in front of *la que*.

pitfalls.right: No vino, lo que me molestó.
pitfalls.why: Almost. To comment on a whole event, you need *lo que*.

pitfalls.wrong: La mujer con el que hablé es periodista.
pitfalls.right: La mujer con la que hablé es periodista.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *El*, *la*, *los*, *las* must match the noun, here *mujer*.

pitfalls.wrong: Nos quedamos sin plata, la que es un problema.
pitfalls.right: Nos quedamos sin plata, lo cual es un problema.
pitfalls.why: Almost. You are commenting on the whole situation, so use *lo cual* or *lo que*.

personal: Say something true about your week and add a comment on it with *lo que*, like *Llegué tarde, lo que…*.
